land.text: Demerara and Essequibo, ceded by the Netherlands: 'The Netherlands officially ceded the three colonies to the United Kingdom' in the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814

predecessors.note: The essequibo dossier ends at 1814-08 (Demerara-Essequibo since 1812); the BG page gives 1814 for the cession and 1815 in its introduction; the treaty was signed in London on 13 August 1814.

land.text: the colony of Berbice, the third of the 'three colonies' ceded in 1814

predecessors.note: The regions are the researcher's reading of the Berbice colony; the BG page gives no boundary between the three colonies.

land.text: 'Guyana became independent of the United Kingdom on 26 May 1966.' At midnight on that date, British Guiana became Guyana.

capitals.name: Georgetown (Stabroek before 1812)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Georgetown; the text says Georgetown "was called Stabroek before 1812". Coordinates from the gazetteer.

correction.text: the three colonies of Demerara, Essequibo and Berbice, 'consolidated into a single colony in 1831', within the Schomburgk line 'declared ... the provisional frontier of British Guiana' in October 1886

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no British Guiana row (the British Colonial Empire row 1706-1999 is an aggregate and its Guiana shapes are not reviewed here). Infobox area 231,800 km2 for 1924; the gazetteer resolves modern Guyana to 825 cells, about 208,600 km2 (ratio 0.90, within a factor of two); the colony of 1924 also held the New River Triangle claimed by Suriname and land later ceded to Brazil, neither measured on the pages opened.

correction.text: after the Paris award of 3 October 1899 gave Britain 'most of the disputed territory and all of the gold mines' and Venezuela Barima Point; the surveyors 'signed off on the border in 1905'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The shape is unchanged from 1814-1898 except for Barima Point (the mouth of the Orinoco) going to Venezuela, a small area the gazetteer cannot name; the 1904 Brazilian arbitration is not on the pages opened.

region.text: Demerara, Essequibo and Berbice, 'the three colonies' ceded by the Netherlands

ledger.note: 13 August 1814: the Netherlands cedes Demerara, Essequibo and Berbice to Britain. The Anglo-Dutch Treaty 'was signed by the [United Kingdom] and the [Netherlands] in London on 13 August 1814'; the British Guiana page: 'The Netherlands officially ceded the three colonies to the United Kingdom' (1814; 1815 in its introduction). Berbice is the berbice dossier's land.

21 July 1831: the three colonies are consolidated as British Guiana. 'The British consolidated the territories into a single colony in 1831'; infobox 'Single colony: 21 July 1831'. The land is unchanged.

region.text: the land west of the Essequibo up to the Orinoco claimed by Venezuela: 'a 159,500 km2 area west of the Essequibo River'

ledger.note: 1895: the Venezuela boundary dispute becomes a crisis. 'The longstanding dispute became a diplomatic crisis in 1895'; in October 1886 Britain had 'declared the Schomburgk Line the provisional frontier of British Guiana'. A diplomatic dispute, not a campaign; the four regions are the researcher's reading of the area west of the river.

region.text: most of the disputed land and all the gold mines, awarded by the Paris tribunal

ledger.note: 3 October 1899: the Paris tribunal awards Britain the Essequibo. 'On 3 October 1899 the Tribunal ruled largely in favour of Britain'; Venezuela received Barima Point, 'control of the Orinoco mouth'. The BG page: 'The tribunal awarded about 94% of the disputed territory to British Guiana.'

region.text: the land west of the Essequibo

ledger.note: 1899: the dispute is settled by arbitration (Treaty of Arbitration signed in Washington on 2 February 1897; Paris award 3 October 1899; border surveyed and 'signed off' in 1905). Venezuela denounced the award at the UN on 12 November 1962.
26 May 1966: British Guiana becomes independent Guyana. 'Guyana became independent of the United Kingdom on 26 May 1966.' The Geneva Agreement on the Venezuelan claim was signed on 17 February 1966.

wars.name: Guyana–Venezuela territorial dispute

zones.text: the Essequibo, 'a 159,500 km2 area west of the Essequibo River'

wars.outcome: Arbitration, not war: Schomburgk surveyed the line in 1840; Britain declared it the provisional frontier in October 1886; the Treaty of Arbitration was signed on 2 February 1897; the Paris award of 3 October 1899 gave Britain most of the land; the frontier was signed off in 1905; Venezuela renewed its claim in 1962 and the Geneva Agreement of 17 February 1966 reopened the matter.
wars.note: Also a claim by the Kingdom of the Netherlands, for Suriname, on the New River Triangle in 1962 (British Guiana page).

certainty.note: The Schomburgk line was only a provisional frontier (1886) and the interior was not surveyed.
The Venezuelan frontier follows the 1899 award, surveyed in 1905; the New River Triangle on the Suriname side and the Brazilian frontier (not on the pages opened) are the exceptions.

notes:
Cliopatria has no row for British Guiana; the Essequibo (1616-1814) and Berbice (1627-1814) rows have dossiers (am-06-c) and end at the cession, and Dutch Suriname (1667-1975) lies to the east. The Cliopatria Guyana row starts in 1967, so this fills 1814-1966. Type colony (a dependency drawn as a vassal tint of the metropole).
Thin or open: the Brazilian frontier (Pirara, 1904 arbitration) and the New River Triangle are not on the pages opened; the Berbice regions and the western Essequibo regions are the researcher's reading of modern Guyana's regions; Barima Point (Orinoco mouth) is not in the gazetteer. The 1814 start month comes from the Anglo-Dutch Treaty page; the BG page gives 1815 in its introduction.
